reference.selected: Linux x86-64 nonblocking Unix WAL VFS; original 32768-byte WAL index regions. Virtual page-size controls are synthetic, not proof of another physical machine.

channel.provenance: Only a fixed trusted dispatcher may wrap actual peer results. Parent input is an already issued HIA DMS-ready node/view, not arbitrary public bytes. Equal headers are not external authentication.

commands.name: INIT
commands.args: q4/q5=0; q6 issued initial source lease; q7 node; q8 issued FS descriptor token or0 process-lock; q9/q10 DB dev/inode; q11 readonly; q12 process-lock; q13 actual OS page size; q14/q15 DMS session nonces; q17 DMS-held1 or process-lock0; q18 actual predecessor node-lease generation; all other fields0
commands.effect: One private mapping session bound to one stable issued DMS node. It does not open/close a descriptor or claim that supplied fields alone authenticate it.

commands.name: MAP
commands.args: q8 region index; q9=32768; q10 bExtend0/1; all other arguments0
commands.effect: DMS retry/held decision must already have completed in the HIA parent. Cached mapping returns immediately; growth follows FSTAT, per-page writes, vector realloc, then one mapping per OS-sized group.

commands.name: PURGE
commands.effect: Called only after last connection removal and any optional unlink. Unmap/free all region groups in ascending order, then free the vector, then retire; parent closes the SHM descriptor after this terminal.

commands.name: BARRIER
commands.effect: Issue memory barrier plus retained global-mutex enter/leave port. This is not implemented as an HIA no-op.

commands.name: PEER_ACK
commands.args: q8 role; q9 operation; q10 errno0..4095; q11 normalized returned value or opaque token; q12 exact result extent; q13 actual invocation serial; q14/q15=0; q17 complete issued request length; q18 result byte length; q19..31=0; payload exact issued request then result bytes
commands.effect: Same call/action/source/node, strictly newer peer serial and exact issued request bytes required before consuming completion once.

commands.name: UNKNOWN
commands.effect: Permanent poison retaining uncertain pending state; never invented retry, allocation, success or release.

commands.name: GROW_ALLOC_FAILED
commands.args: current call/action/lease/node; q8=12; no other argument/body
commands.effect: Only while an index-workspace GROW is pending. Return IOERR_NOMEM preserving old mapped regions/table and completed file writes.

output.why_257: A raw PWRITE request carries the original one NUL byte. This is a private ABI minimum, not a bound on user data, mappings, nodes or database size.

statuses.2: GROW same immutable input; no peer replay

issued.body: Only FS PWRITE emits one zero byte

output.view: The result identifies an issued mapping token plus range. It is not a raw pointer and grants no access without the actual fixed memory registry and parent-issued view.

3.name: one raw PWRITE
3.success: count0/1, no body; EINTR retry is decided by this HIA owner

15.name: full x86-64 FSTAT
15.success: value0, extent144, actual 144-byte stat at result; st_size offset48

1.name: REALLOC_VECTOR
1.success: opaque vector token and exact requested extent; prior vector remains valid on failure; success may preserve the same token/address

2.name: MMAP_FILE
2.success: fresh live mapping lease and exact extent; underlying operation MAP_SHARED

3.name: ALLOC_ZERO
3.success: fresh zeroed heap lease, same complete requested extent

4.name: MUNMAP
4.success: one raw unmap attempt; Linux rounds nominal length to OS page size; known failure is ignored by original purge but logical view retired

5.name: FREE
5.success: retire once; preserve any actual cleanup error as ignored observation

6.name: BARRIER
6.success: actual compiler/hardware memory barrier and retained namespace global mutex enter/leave; cannot be a synthetic success in physical qualification

ports.unknown: The fixed provider and HIA registry must issue roles, tokens, bytes, serials and actual statuses. This component's fake replies do not qualify those providers.

fields.8: phase1 idle/2 peer/3 parent GROW/4 ACK GROW/6 retired/7 poison

record: opaque mapping token, zero only after its known purge completion
number of logical regions in this mapping
state.bounds: Every record range is validated before lookup. A complete pending stage/op/role/arguments and saved issued-request frame are cross-checked. No fixed global region/node/byte count limit.
state.growth: Required state/index bytes use checked u64 arithmetic; same full immutable source view must survive GROW. Only its header is compared locally, so this is a private fixed-lease prerequisite.
state.retirement: Purge consumes each known release once, ignores its recorded errors like the retained caller, frees vector last, and permanently retires this node mapping session.

order: Cached region returns without FSTAT, vector realloc or mmap.
Assign szRegion before the first FSTAT; FSTAT error gives IOERR_SHMSIZE.
Too-small file with !bExtend returns NULL/OK, then READONLY conversion if applicable; no vector allocation.
Extend with exactly one NUL at each 4096-byte page tail, starting floor(oldSize/4096); retry only PWRITE EINTR, zero write stops.
Allocate/reallocate pointer-vector capacity after all file writes; failure IOERR_NOMEM keeps old vector/mappings and already written file.
Each file group mmap failure yields IOERR_SHMMAP; process-lock zeroed allocation failure yields NOMEM; earlier successful groups remain live.
Readonly converts only an otherwise OK MAP result to READONLY, while retaining a valid returned view when mapped.
Purge happens after unlink and before descriptor close in the parent; this owner never opens/closes/unlinks itself.

limits_and_equivalence.address_overflow: Explicit NEW defensive behavior at impossible u64 address overflow is IOERR_NOMEM. It is not claimed equivalent to original C signed-overflow/undefined inputs; this does not remove any defined ordinary caller behavior.
limits_and_equivalence.C_storage_width: Private state uses u64 and does not assert equivalence for original C nByte overflow or nRegion truncation beyond the original defined size domain.
limits_and_equivalence.allocator_failure: Test fixtures model actual issued allocation failure receipts. The fixed physical allocator, recovery after infrastructure allocation failure, and all real mappings remain unqualified.

planned_tests.semantic_basis: Assertions derived from retained C branches; CoreVM/native equality is not itself a retained-C oracle or physical qualification.
